text:
amy-support: heads up — acme (ticket C-9342) reporting intermittent high tail latency on /v1/embeddings. normally ~20-60ms, but seeing 2s+ and occasional 10s spikes. they also reported some dim-mismatch 400s

acme-rep: we haven't changed client, still sending 512-dim vectors. errors show: "vector dim 384 != expected 512" for a small subset. most requests succeed. attaching a minimal repro: many single-item requests sent rapidly from mobile.

mike-ingest: can you paste the exact request headers and a sample payload? also any x-request-id from failed requests?

acme-rep: sample curl pasted below (we redacted keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Client-Batch-Hint: 1' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small-512","inputs":["hello world"]}' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: acme-20260316-1'
```

mike-ingest: thanks. two things to check: 1) the dim-mismatch usually means the client sent a different model/embedding vector to a rerank or store endpoint — but if it's our embeddings API returning that, likely a downstream batching/shard routing mixing model variants. 2) the tail spikes line up with dynbatch coalescing windows when we saw many 1-item requests. runtime-bot: embed-queue alert fired 2026-03-16T12:15:04Z (queue depth 256, tail p99 9.8s).

runtime-bot: alert details -> https://observability.internal/alerts/AL-embed-queue-2177 (auto note)

olivia-eng: I pulled the logs for the timeframe. the router temporarily routed requests to a mixed-variant shard while a canary rollout was in progress — some instances still had embed-small-384 (old variant). That explains the dim mismatch for a tiny subset. The tail latency is separate: dynbatch max_batch_size was 128 and max_wait_ms 20. With lots of 1-item mobile calls, we saw a fill/flush pathology where a few large batches block the slot and small requests wait for max_wait_ms, causing long tails.

mike-ingest: reproduction steps for support to gather traces: ask customer to send 10 requests with incremental X-Request-ID and include header `X-Debug=embed-batching`. Have them run at ~50 qps for 30s to trigger coalescing. Capture the request ids for us.

amy-support: noted. I've asked acme to run the mini-repro and provide the ids. temporary mitigation we can recommend to them: set `X-Client-Batch-Hint: 8` or batch client-side to avoid many single-item calls. Also we can patch our routing to avoid mixing model variants mid-rollout (OLIVIA to follow).

olivia-eng: short-term config change we can push to Dedicated/Hosted: reduce dynbatch `max_wait_ms` to 8 for embed routes and set `max_batch_size` to 64 for the model shard that is noisy. This reduces p99 but slightly increases total token cost due to more smaller batches. We'll run A/B on a small fleet first.

mike-ingest: engineering note: we'll also emit a metric `batch_wait_time_by_client` so we can detect clients that cause chronic coalescing and issue guidance.

amy-support: acme provided three trace ids: acme-20260316-1, acme-20260316-4, acme-20260316-7. I uploaded them to the internal trace viewer.

olivia-eng: I inspected acme-20260316-4 — shows routing to embed-small-384 for one request, everything else to 512. That confirms mixed-variant routing bug. I'll open PR to ensure shard compatibility checks before forwarding — target PR today.

mike-ingest: for support playbook: 1) ask for X-Request-IDs, 2) check model variant on shard in router logs, 3) suggest client-side batching or header hint, 4) if tail spike, consider temporary dynbatch tweak (max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_size=64), 5) escalate to eng-runtime if mixed variants found.

amy-support: thanks — I'll send acme the recommended mitigations and mark the ticket as escalated to eng-runtime. please ping here with PR/rollout ETA so I can update the customer. :thumbsup:
